rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands Adam, Eve, and Iblis all to descend from Paradise; Ibn Kathir says the matter was treated at length in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى لآدم وحواء وإبليس: اهبطوا منها جميعا، أي: من الجنة كلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enemies are Adam and his descendants on one side, and Iblis and his descendants on the other.
rows.anchor: {بعضكم لبعض عدو} قال: آدم وذريته، وإبليس وذريته

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya identifies the promised guidance as the prophets, messengers, and clear explanation.
rows.anchor: قال أبو العالية: الأنبياء والرسل والبيان

words: فَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا يَضِلُّ وَلَا يَشْقَىٰ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the follower of God's guidance does not go astray in this life or suffer in the next.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لا يضل في الدنيا، ولا يشقى في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away from God's reminder means opposing His command and revelation to His messenger, neglecting it, and taking guidance from elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أي: خالف أمري، وما أنزلته على رسولي، أعرض عنه وتناساه وأخذ من غيره هداه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The constricted life is worldly inward distress: no tranquility or open heart, but anxiety, doubt, and uncertainty, even amid outward luxury.
rows.anchor: أي: في الدنيا، فلا طمأنينة له، ولا انشراح لصدره، بل صدره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in a report transmitted by Ali ibn Abi Talha, glosses the constricted life as misery.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Awfi transmits Ibn Abbas as saying that wealth, little or much, brings no good if its recipient does not fear God; this is constricted living.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some deniers had worldly abundance yet a constricted life: they distrusted God to sustain them, and their disbelief and poor expectation made life difficult.
rows.anchor: ويقال: إن قوما ضلالا أعرضوا عن الحق، وكانوا في سعة من الدنيا متكبرين

rows.speaker: الضحاك، عكرمة، مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak, Ikrima, and Malik ibn Dinar each explain the constricted living as evil deeds and corrupt provision.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: هو العمل السيئ، والرزق الخبيث، وكذا قال عكرمة، ومالك بن دينار

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id says the constricted life is the grave squeezing its occupant until his ribs press against each other.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد في قوله: {معيشة ضنكا} قال: يضيق عليه قبره، حتى تختلف أضلاعه فيه

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم الرازي
rows.claim: Abu Hatim al-Razi identifies al-Nu'man ibn Abi Ayyash as kunya Abu Salama, the transmitter named in the preceding report.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حاتم الرازي: النعمان بن أبي عياش (3) يكنى أبا سلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from Abu Sa'id a Prophetic gloss, grave squeeze; Ibn Kathir says the stopped version is more authentic.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قول الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet describing the believer's spacious, lit grave and the unbeliever's grave torment by ninety-nine many-headed dragons; Ibn Kathir calls this raised version very munkar.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: المؤمن في قبره في روضة خضراء

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar transmits Abu Hurayra's Prophetic explanation that constricted living is punishment by ninety-nine snakes biting the sinner until resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قول الله عز وجل: {فإن له معيشة ضنكا} قال

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A second report from Abu Hurayra identifies the constricted living as grave punishment; Ibn Kathir grades its chain good.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سلمة، عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد، أبو صالح، السدي
rows.claim: Mujahid, Abu Salih, and al-Suddi say the person will have no proof or argument.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، وأبو صالح، والسدي: لا حجة له

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says everything will be obscured from him except Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: عمي عليه كل شيء إلا جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir considers that the denier is raised or brought to the Fire blind in sight and insight, as in 17:97.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون المراد: أنه يحشر أو يبعث (3) إلى النار أعمى البصر والبصيرة أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier asks why he was gathered blind when he had sight in worldly life.
rows.anchor: ولهذا يقول: {رب لم حشرتني أعمى وقد كنت بصيرا} أي: في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's signs had come to him, but he treated them as if he did not remember them, deliberately neglecting and ignoring them after they were conveyed.
rows.anchor: لما أعرضت عن آيات الله، وعاملتها معاملة من لم يذكرها، بعد بلاغها إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God treats him as forgotten in return, as in the verse that says He forgets them as they forgot their meeting with this Day.
rows.anchor: فاليوم ننساهم كما نسوا لقاء يومهم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recompense matches the deed.
rows.anchor: فإن الجزاء من جنس العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting Quranic wording while understanding its meaning and observing it is outside this particular threat, though another threat applies and the Sunnah warns severely against it.
rows.anchor: فأما نسيان لفظ القرآن مع فهم معناه والقيام بمقتضاه، فليس داخلا في هذا الوعيد الخاص

rows.speaker: سعد بن عبادة
rows.claim: Ahmad transmits from Sa'd ibn Ubada that a man who reads the Quran and then forgets it will meet God with the condition described as ajdham.
rows.anchor: عن رجل، عن سعد بن عبادة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
rows.claim: Ahmad also gives the same Prophetic warning through Ubadah ibn al-Samit instead of Sa'd ibn Ubada.
rows.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فذكر مثله سواء

words: مَنْ أَسْرَفَ وَلَمْ يُؤْمِنۢ بِـَٔايَٰتِ رَبِّهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God requites profligate deniers of His signs in this life and the next, as also stated in 13:34.
rows.anchor: يقول تعالى: وهكذا نجازي المسرفين المكذبين بآيات الله في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife's punishment is more painful than worldly punishment and lasts longer; its people remain in it forever.
rows.anchor: أي: أشد ألما من عذاب الدنيا، وأدوم عليهم، فهم مخلدون فيه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told the spouses involved in mutual imprecation that the punishment of this world is easier than that of the next.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم للمتلاعنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers ask why Muhammad does not bring a sign from his Lord, meaning a mark that proves he is God's messenger.
rows.anchor: بعلامة دالة على صدقه في أنه رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof is the revealed Quran: Muhammad was unlettered, had not studied with the People of the Book, yet it tells earlier histories in agreement with authentic prior scriptures, confirms what is true, and exposes their false additions.
rows.anchor: يعني: القرآن العظيم الذي أنزله عليه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument parallels 29:50–51: the Quran recited to them should suffice as a mercy and reminder for believers.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية كقوله تعالى في سورة "العنكبوت"

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said every prophet received signs like those that led people to believe, while his own gift was revelation from God, and he hoped for the largest following on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيح عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies the Quran as Muhammad's greatest sign and says he had countless other miracles, documented elsewhere in the books.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر هاهنا أعظم الآيات التي أعطيها، عليه السلام، وهو القرآن

words: ولو أنا أهلكناهم بعذاب من قبله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had God destroyed the deniers before sending the messenger and revelation, they could have protested that a messenger should first have been sent so they could follow the signs before humiliation.
rows.anchor: ولو أنا أهلكناهم بعذاب من قبله لقالوا ربنا لولا أرسلت إلينا رسولا

words: فنتبع آياتك من قبل أن نذل ونخزى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the deniers obstinate: no sign would make them believe until they saw painful punishment, citing 10:97, 6:155–157, 35:42, and 6:109–110.
rows.anchor: يبين تعالى أن هؤلاء المكذبين متعنتون معاندون لا يؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to say that both sides, the believers and the deniers, are waiting, so they should wait for the outcome.
rows.anchor: أي: منا ومنكم {فتربصوا} أي: فانتظروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sound path is the straight road; the guided person is one who reached truth and the way of right direction.
rows.anchor: أي: الطريق المستقيم، {ومن اهتدى} إلى الحق وسبيل الرشاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning resembles 25:42, where they will learn who is farther astray, and 54:26, which says they will know who is the great liar.
rows.anchor: وهذا كقوله (1) تعالى {وسوف يعلمون حين يرون العذاب من أضل سبيلا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains anchor and weigh down the earth to keep it from swaying; Ibn Kathir adds that water covers it except for about a quarter exposed to air and sun, allowing inhabitants to see the sky and its signs.
rows.anchor: أي: جبالا أرسى الأرض بها وقررها وثقلها؛ لئلا تميد بالناس، أي: تضطرب وتتحرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountain gaps make routes between regions and lands, letting people cross barriers and find their way.
rows.anchor: أي: ثغرا في الجبال، يسلكون فيها طرقا من قطر إلى قطر، وإقليم إلى إقليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is a roof over earth shaped like a dome, as also described in 51:47, 91:5, and 50:6.
rows.anchor: أي: على الأرض وهي كالقبة عليها، كما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir explains building as raising a dome, likens the Prophet's saying that Islam was built on five to five supports, and describes this as familiar tent construction among Arabs.
rows.anchor: والبناء هو نصب القبة، كما قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is high and guarded against being reached.
rows.anchor: أي: عاليا محروسا أن ينال. وقال مجاهد: مرفوعا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses the sky as raised.
rows.anchor: أي: عاليا محروسا أن ينال. وقال مجاهد: مرفوعا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits a Prophetic description of the sky as a wave held back from people; Ibn Kathir calls its chain unusual.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال رجل: يا رسول الله، ما هذه السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People fail to reflect on the sky's vastness and height, its fixed and wandering stars, and the sun's immense daily and nightly course; see 12:105.
rows.anchor: أي: لا يتفكرون فيما خلق الله فيها من الاتساع العظيم، والارتفاع الباهر

rows.speaker: ابن أبي الدنيا
rows.claim: Ibn Abi al-Dunya recounts an Israelite worshiper who received no cloud after thirty years; his mother concluded that he often looked skyward and lowered his eyes without reflection, which he admitted.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر ابن أبي الدنيا، رحمه الله، في كتابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is dark and still while day brings light and ease; each alternately lengthens and shortens.
rows.anchor: هذا في ظلامه وسكونه، وهذا بضيائه وأنسه، يطول هذا تارة ثم يقصر أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun and moon each have distinct light, orbit, time, movement, course, and measure.
rows.anchor: هذه لها نور يخصها، وفلك بذاته، وزمان على حدة، وحركة وسير خاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means they revolve; the verse also links to 36:40 and God's calculation of night and day and the sun and moon in 6:96.
rows.anchor: {وكل في فلك يسبحون} [يس:40] ، أي: يدورون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid compare the celestial bodies' rotation to a spindle turning in its whorl, with each turning in relation to the other.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يدورون كما يدور المغزل في الفلكة. وكذا قال مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the Jonah story also appears in al-Saffat and Nun; God sent Jonah son of Matta to Nineveh near Mosul, whose people rejected his call.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن يونس بن متى، عليه السلام، بعثه الله إلى أهل قرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah left his people angrily after warning them of punishment in three days; believing a prophet would not lie, they went into the wilderness with their children and herds, separated mothers and young, cried to God, and were spared, as in 10:98.
rows.anchor: فلما تحققوا منه ذلك، وعلموا أن النبي لا يكذب، خرجوا إلى الصحراء بأطفالهم وأنعامهم ومواشيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah sailed with others, and when they feared the vessel would sink, lots were drawn three times to choose someone to cast away; each time they fell on him, as in 37:141.
rows.anchor: فاقترعوا على رجل يلقونه من بينهم يتخففون منه، فوقعت القرعة على يونس

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud is cited for the whale being sent from the Green Sea.
rows.anchor: من البحر الأخضر -فيما قاله ابن مسعود-حوتا يشق البحار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Jonah threw himself into the sea, the whale swallowed him; God ordered it not to eat his flesh or break his bones, since its belly was to be a prison for Jonah, not his food.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله إلى ذلك الحوت ألا تأكل له لحما، ولا تهشم له عظما؛ فإن يونس ليس لك رزقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhun-Nun means the whale; the possessive association is valid because of their relation.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {وذا النون} يعني: الحوت، صحت الإضافة إليه بهذه النسبة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says Jonah left angrily toward his people.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {إذ ذهب مغاضبا} : قال الضحاك: لقومه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، الضحاك، ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and others explain the phrase as thinking God would not constrict him in the whale; Ibn Kathir notes Ibn Jarir prefers this, citing 65:7.
rows.anchor: يروى نحو هذا عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والضحاك، وغيرهم، واختاره (7) ابن جرير

rows.speaker: عطية العوفي
rows.claim: Atiyya al-Awfi reads the phrase as thinking God would not decree against him; he takes qadara and qaddara as synonyms, citing Arabic usage, a poem, and 54:12.
rows.anchor: وقال عطية العوفي: {فظن أن لن نقدر عليه} (8) ، أي: نقضي عليه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the darknesses as the whale's belly, the sea, and night.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: ظلمة بطن الحوت، وظلمة البحر، وظلمة الليل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، عمرو بن ميمون، سعيد بن جبير، محمد بن كعب، الضحاك، الحسن، قتادة
rows.claim: The same three darknesses are also reported from Ibn Abbas, Amr ibn Maymun, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, and Qatada.
rows.anchor: وكذا روي عن ابن عباس (1) ، وعمرو بن ميمون، وسعيد بن جبير، ومحمد بن كعب، والضحاك، والحسن، وقتادة

rows.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
rows.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd says the darkness was a whale inside another whale, in the darkness of the sea.
rows.anchor: وقال سالم بن أبي الجعد: ظلمة حوت في بطن حوت (2) ، في ظلمة البحر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود، ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and others say the whale carried Jonah through the seas to the bottom, where he heard the pebbles glorifying God and prayed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود، وابن عباس وغيرهما: وذلك أنه ذهب به الحوت في البحار يشقها، حتى انتهى به إلى قرار البحر، فسمع (3) يونس تسبيح الحصى

rows.speaker: عوف
rows.claim: Awf says Jonah thought he had died, moved his legs, then prostrated and called the whale's belly a prayer place where no one else had prayed.
rows.anchor: وقال عوف: لما صار يونس في بطن الحوت، ظن أنه قد مات، ثم حرك رجليه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن أبي الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri says Jonah remained in the whale's belly for forty days; Ibn Jubayr narrates both this and the preceding report.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن أبي الحسن البصري: مكث في بطن الحوت أربعين يوما. رواهما (7) ابن جبير

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying the whale spared Jonah and he heard sea creatures glorify God; angels recognized his voice, recalled his daily righteous deeds, interceded, and God ordered him cast ashore sick (37:145). Al-Bazzar says the report is known only through this route.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن رافع -مولى أم سلمة-سمعت أبا هريرة يقول: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports a Prophetic warning that a servant should not claim superiority to Jonah son of Matta, who glorified God in the darknesses.
rows.anchor: عن علي مرفوعا: لا ينبغي لعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding hadith also circulates without the clause comparing oneself to Jonah, on routes from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud, and Abdullah ibn Ja'far; further chains appear in Surat Nun.
rows.anchor: وقد روي هذا الحديث بدون هذه الزيادة، من حديث ابن عباس، وابن مسعود، وعبد الله بن جعفر

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas tentatively raises a report to the Prophet: Jonah prayed the supplication in the whale, and it rose toward the Throne as angels heard a faint, familiar voice from a strange land.
rows.anchor: أنس بن مالك -ولا أعلم إلا أن أنسا يرفع الحديث إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم- أن يونس النبي

words: لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: In Anas's report, God identifies Jonah as a servant whose accepted deeds and answered prayers were known to the angels; they ask God to show mercy in adversity because of his ease-time worship, and the whale casts him ashore.
rows.anchor: أنس بن مالك -ولا أعلم إلا أن أنسا يرفع الحديث إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم- أن يونس النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered Jonah by bringing him out of the whale's belly and the darknesses.
rows.anchor: أي: أخرجناه من بطن الحوت، وتلك الظلمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God likewise rescues believers when hardship drives them to call on Him in repentance; the Prophet encouraged this supplication, especially in distress.
rows.anchor: أي: إذا كانوا في الشدائد ودعونا منيبين إلينا، ولا سيما إذا دعوا بهذا الدعاء في حال البلاء

words: لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas tells how Uthman failed to return his greeting, Umar asked about it, and Uthman recalled that remembering a Prophetic saying made his sight and heart grow clouded.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه سعد، -وهو ابن أبي وقاص -قال: مررت بعثمان بن عفان، رضي الله عنه، في المسجد

words: لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنتَ سُبْحَٰنَكَ إِنِّى كُنتُ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet identifies Jonah's prayer in the whale and says no Muslim invokes God with it about any matter without being answered; Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas transmits the report.
rows.anchor: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر لنا [أول دعوة]
